messages:
Anya: Quick post-launch sync — need to decide scope for the next two sprints. We got 3 P1s (dedicated customers), ~8 P2s, and a pile of small UX asks. Proposal: 1-week hotfix sprint to clear P1s + critical P2s, then a 2-week follow-on focusing on quick wins + backlog items. Opinions?
Mike: +1 for hotfix sprint. P1s sound like regressions; we should triage and patch fast. We can bundle 2 P2s if small.
Sam: FYI the P1s are: customer A failing auth with dedicated VPC, customer B seeing model mismatch on quantized models, customer C huge latency spikes during bursts. All flagged as blocking.
Elaine: Some of the UX asks are purely client-side text + microcopy, 1-2 dev days each. We could knock 3 of them in the 2-week sprint if we reserve capacity.
Ben: Suggest we use a simple prioritization rubric so we don't argue in the sprint:
```
- Severity: P1 (customer production broken) > P2 (degraded) > P3 (nuisance)
- Reach: number of customers impacted
- Repro: deterministic > intermittent
- Effort: <2d quick wins get a higher chance
- Strategic: customer is enterprise / SLA / in pilot -> bump priority
```
Kate: From platform side, we need a canary rollout for the auth fix (P1). I can own the canary and rollback hooks. Will need 2 engineers for the patch + one SRE on-call.
Mike: Agree. Engineering estimate: P1 auth fix ~2 dev days + testing, quantized mismatch ~3 days (investigation), latency bursts needs perf traces first (1 day to instrument).
Anya: So practical plan:
- Sprint 1 (hotfix, 1 week): owner Mike + Kate -> auth fix (P1), perf tracing + mitigation (P1 candidate), immediate patch for model mismatch if we confirm repro. Reserve 40% eng time for testing/canaries.
- Sprint 2 (2 weeks): focus on 3 quick UX wins (Elaine + 1 dev), 2 medium P2s, and top backlog items based on rubric.
Sam: Customers A/B/C want ETA. Can we commit to hotfix release by end of next week?
Mike: If we start tomorrow and parallelize, yes for auth fix. Quant mismatch might slip one additional week depending on repro.
Ben: We should also gate enhancements by measurable acceptance criteria — e.g., "reduced end-to-end time by X" or "no regression on canary".
Elaine: For the UX quick wins, I'll write tiny specs tomorrow morning and mark as "low effort" in the ticket.
Anya: Action items:
- Mike: triage P1s, assign PR owners, target hotfix by Fri (owner: Mike).
- Kate: set up canary and rollback, coordinate testing windows (owner: Kate).
- Elaine: spec 3 quick UX fixes and link tickets (owner: Elaine).
- Ben: run rubric across backlog and return top 10 candidates (owner: Ben).
- Sam: notify customers with a soft ETA + ask for repro details if available (owner: Sam).
Please reply with any blockers by EOD.
Mike: I'll post a short triage doc in the thread after the stand.
Elaine: :thumbsup:
Ben: If we end up with leftover capacity in sprint 2, prefer small enhancements that reduce token cost or improve latency. Those have biggest unit-economics impact.
Anya: Okay — two checkpoints: triage meeting tomorrow 10:30 and sprint kickoff on Mon.
ops-bot: Deploy window reserved: Fri 22:00 UTC -> 23:30 UTC. Canary slots: 22:15, rollback window 22:45.
Sam: I'll schedule the customer updates after we confirm the Friday window.
Anya: Thanks everyone. If no objections, I'll lock the plan at 17:00 and create the sprint cards.
Mike: No objections from eng. Lock it.
Kate: Ready on infra side.
Ben: Done on my end.
Elaine: 👍
Anya: Locking plan. I'll follow up with the sprint board and owners.
